paper_metadata.title: Structure and mechanical properties of a refractory Al7.5(NbTiZr)92.5 medium-entropy alloy subjected to long-term annealing and oxidation

evidence.quote: Recently, Al-containing refractory high/medium-entropy alloys (RH/MEAs) have attracted special attention from materials scientists worldwide.

parameters.atmosphere: vacuumed (10^-2 torr) quartz tubes filled with titanium chips

evidence.quote: For phase stability evaluation, a long-term (500 h) annealing at 600, 700, or 800 °C was performed. Prior to the annealing, the samples were encapsulated in vacuumed (10-2 torr) quartz tubes filled with titanium chips to prevent contamination with impurities. The encapsulated samples were then put into a preheated Nabertherm furnace and held for 500 h, followed by quenching in water.

the microstructure of the Al7.5(NbTiZr)92.5 alloy consisted of polygonal-shaped bcc grains with an average size of ~20 – 25 μm.

attributes.location: homogeneously distributed within the bcc grains

evidence.quote: TEM studies in a dark-field (DF) regime under the {001} superlattice reflection of the [011]bcc zone axis (ZA) revealed multiple (volume fraction, f, of ≈ 30 %), round-shaped, and nanosized (d ≈ 0.8 – 0.9 nm) B2 domains homogeneously distributed within the bcc grains

attributes.morphology: lenticular/round-like shape; grain boundary particles created almost continuous networks/interlayers; grain interior particles formed heterogeneously distributed agglomerates/clusters

evidence.quote: The total volume fraction and average size (transversal) of particles were estimated as ~16 % and ~0.3 μm, respectively.
the particles were larger (~2 μm), while their volume fraction was much lower (~3 %).
a tiny (~0.5 %) volume fraction of secondary phase particles was observed. Unlike 600 and 700 °C, the particles distributed homogeneously, without the preferred location at grain boundaries
SEM-BSE and SEM-EDS images showed the formation of non-compact oxide layers (OL) having homogeneous distribution of the elements at all the temperatures.

mechanisms.name: premature macroscopic localisation of plastic deformation

evidence.quote: The oxidation for 1 h decreased the room-temperature ductility owing to the premature macroscopic localisation of plastic deformation induced by synergistic effects from the volumetric (Al,Nb,Ti,Zr)O4 oxide.
